Inspect long-format data before fitting an mvgam

Source: R/mvgam_data.R
mvgam_data.Rd

Runs the checks mvgam() applies to its data before compiling a model. It tests the columns, factor levels, time spacing and response support of a proposed model. A failure raises the error mvgam() would raise. An optional plot shows each observed series.

Usage

mvgam_data(
  data,
  y = NULL,
  family = gaussian(),
  formula = NULL,
  trend_formula = NULL,
  data2 = NULL,
  plot = TRUE,
  newdata = NULL,
  series = NULL,
  lines = TRUE,
  n_bins = NULL,
  log_scale = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Long-format data.frame (or list) carrying at least the response column and a time column. A latent trend also needs each row's series: a series column, the column the trend constructor's series argument names, or the gr and subgr columns of a hierarchical trend. Closure-unit families (occ(), nmix()) always require series and visit columns. A family without a default cap also requires a cap column.

y

Optional name of the response column. NULL (default) takes the response of formula, or "y" when formula is NULL. A name that differs from the response of formula is refused.

family

A family, brmsfamily or mvgam family object. Defaults to gaussian(). The response must lie in the family's support, such as non-negative integers for poisson() or (0, 1) for Beta(). A cap column must hold integers no smaller than the response and stay constant within a closure unit. Multi-response families (diri(), multi(), categ(), mvn(), mvt()) are refused. mvgam() and jsdgam() check their data at fit time.

formula

Optional observation formula, as a formula or a brmsformula. A closure-unit family takes a detection formula in the same bf(). Every column the formula uses must be in data. These include covariates, offsets, random-effect grouping factors and the columns of addition terms such as trials() and weights(). Those columns may not hold NA. A trials() count may not fall below its response. A missing response is allowed. mvgam() keeps its row on the time grid.

trend_formula

Optional trend formula (e.g. ~ AR(time = week, series = species) + s(env)), as passed to mvgam(). Its trend constructor names the time and series columns and decides whether times must be evenly spaced: CAR() and ZMVN() accept gaps, most others refuse them. NULL checks the data for a model without a trend, which needs no series column. Its covariates, offsets and grouping factors get the same checks as those of formula.

data2

Optional named list of further model data, as passed to mvgam(). A formula variable found here, such as a matrix covariate, need not be a column of data.

plot

Logical. TRUE (default) draws the observed series with the panels of plot(fit, type = "series"). Several series draw as one facet each. One series draws four panels: the time series, a histogram, the ACF and the empirical CDF.

newdata

Optional held-out data in the long format of data. The time series panels draw it in black after a dashed line at the first test time. The histogram, ACF and CDF of one series pool the training and test values.

series

Series to plot: NULL, "all", a series name or a positive index into the series levels. NULL draws every series of multi-series data and the one series otherwise. Data without a series column plot as one series named after the response.

lines

Logical. Plot lines (default) or points.

n_bins

Optional histogram bin count.

log_scale

Logical. Plot the response as log(y + 1).

Value

Invisibly, an mvgam_data list with elements data (the validated data), family (the resolved family), series_levels

(NULL when the data name no series), n_series, time_range, n_obs, n_missing (the count of missing responses) and plot

(the ggplot or patchwork object when plot = TRUE, else NULL). With plot = TRUE the plot is also drawn on the active device.

See also

mvgam(), mvgam_formula(), jsdgam(), sim_mvgam(), sim_closure_unit_data(), get_prior.mvgam_formula().

Other model fitting: check_newdata(), jsdgam(), mvgam(), mvgam_formula(), mvgam_multiple(), pivot_detection_array(), pivot_species_matrix(), series_to_mvgam(), stancode.mvgam_formula(), update.mvgam()

Author

Nicholas J Clark

Examples

set.seed(1)
simdat <- sim_mvgam(family = poisson(), n_series = 3L,
                    n_timepoints = 60L)

# Check the frame for a Poisson trend model and plot every series
mvgam_data(simdat$data_train, family = poisson(),
           trend_formula = ~ AR())
#> ✔ Data check passed for family 'poisson (link = log)'.
#> • series: 3 levels
#> • time:   1 to 45
#> • n obs:  135 (0 NA)


# One series in four panels: time series, histogram, ACF and ECDF.
# The test data follow the dashed line.
mvgam_data(simdat$data_train, family = poisson(), series = 1L,
           newdata = simdat$data_test)
#> ✔ Data check passed for family 'poisson (link = log)'.
#> • series: 3 levels
#> • time:   1 to 45
#> • n obs:  135 (0 NA)


# A response the family cannot take is refused before any Stan
# compile. The error names the column, the values and the support.
counts <- simdat$data_train
counts$y[3L] <- -1
try(mvgam_data(counts, family = poisson(), plot = FALSE))
#> Error : 'y' has values outside the support of family 'poisson'.
#>   Requires: 0 <= 'y' (integers only).
#>   Observed range: [-1, 26]. 1 of 135 values fall outside, the first at row
#>   3.
#>   Check the column for missing-data sentinels such as -1 or -999.

# AR() assumes evenly spaced times. CAR() models the gaps.
gappy <- simdat$data_train[simdat$data_train$time != 5L, ]
try(mvgam_data(gappy, family = poisson(), trend_formula = ~ AR(),
               plot = FALSE))
#> Error : The trend needs regularly spaced times in 'time'.
#>   Gaps between times range from 1 to 2.
#>   Add the missing times as rows with an NA response.
#>   'CAR()' models a trend over irregular times.
mvgam_data(gappy, family = poisson(), trend_formula = ~ CAR(),
           plot = FALSE)
#> ✔ Data check passed for family 'poisson (link = log)'.
#> • series: 3 levels
#> • time:   1 to 45
#> • n obs:  132 (0 NA)
